items.defectStatement: Both close() and terminate() shut down the factory-owned queue pool that subsequent strategies reuse. After rebalance, submissions to that pool fail, and submit() incorrectly marks those unprocessed messages complete.
obligations: Leave the shared queue pool usable when an individual strategy closes or terminates.
Stop the retiring strategy's commit thread before teardown returns so it cannot keep invoking its stale callback.
Preserve queued work and leave pool shutdown to its owner.
items.notes: The factory already shuts down its pool. Removing only the shutdown calls fixes pool reuse, but retaining a timed join can leave a stale commit callback running. Partition-generation isolation and submission-error handling are separate issues.

items.defectStatement: submit() sends FilteredPayload to the factory decoder, which asserts against that payload type, routing intentional filtering through exception handling. A filtered payload wrapped in BrokerValue still has its offset completed by that handler, so the finding's blanket claim that filtered offsets are never tracked is incorrect.
obligations: Recognize FilteredPayload before invoking the decoder.
Record and complete the broker offset of a filtered message without enqueueing work or logging a submission failure.
Preserve decoding, grouping, and queue submission for ordinary payloads.
Preserve the existing handling of decoder results that are None.
items.exampleFix:
def submit(self, message: Message[KafkaPayload | FilteredPayload]) -> None:
        try:
            result = None if isinstance(message.payload, FilteredPayload) else self.decoder(message.payload)

            assert isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue)
            partition = message.value.partition
            offset = message.value.offset

            if result is None:
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(partition, offset)
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(partition, offset)
                return

            group_key = self.grouping_fn(result)

            work_item = WorkItem(
                partition=partition,
                offset=offset,
                result=result,
                message=message,
            )

            self.queue_pool.submit(group_key, work_item)

        except Exception:
            logger.exception("Error submitting message to queue")
            if isinstance(message.value, BrokerValue):
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.add_offset(
                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
                )
                self.queue_pool.offset_tracker.complete_offset(
                    message.value.partition, message.value.offset
                )
items.notes: Check message.payload, not whether message.value is FilteredPayload. The repository test constructs BrokerValue(FilteredPayload(), ...). Broader support for non-BrokerValue messages is not established by this finding.

items.defectStatement: The error-handling test checks for absent commits only 0.2 seconds after processing attempts, before the one-second commit loop normally runs. It therefore passes even though the current worker completes both offsets and subsequently commits next-read offset 102.
obligations: Observe the expected commit outcome, or synchronize an actual commit attempt before asserting that no commit occurred.
Fail on timeout instead of treating an unobserved commit cycle as success.
Retain verification that both processing attempts occurred.
items.exampleFix:
if (
                    stats["total_items"] == 0
                    and mock_processor_call.call_count >= 2
                    and committed_offsets.get(test_partition) == 102
                ):
                    break
                time.sleep(0.1)

            assert mock_processor_call.call_count == 2
            assert test_partition in committed_offsets
            assert committed_offsets[test_partition] == 102
items.notes: This example follows the finding's proposed assertion and characterizes current behavior. It conflicts with #03's success-only policy. A regression test for that policy should instead synchronize a commit attempt and assert the failed offset remains uncommitted; that test should fail on the current implementation.

items.defectStatement: _commit_loop() invokes Arroyo's commit callback from a background thread while the consumer thread can poll or revoke partitions. This permits concurrent access to consumer state and commits using a retiring strategy's callback.
obligations: Invoke the commit callback on the consumer thread through its strategy lifecycle methods.
Continue advancing eligible offsets while the strategy is active.
Mark tracker offsets committed only after the callback succeeds.
Prevent deferred commits from surviving the strategy's ownership lifecycle.
items.notes: Changing only the background loop cannot establish a consumer-thread commit path; poll/submit and lifecycle wiring must also change. Merely deleting commits loses progress, and a lock used only by the background thread provides no protection.

items.defectStatement: FixedQueuePool creates unbounded queues, and submit() always accepts additional work without applying backpressure. When workers fall behind, retained work items can grow without limit.
obligations: Enforce a finite bound on queued work.
Apply backpressure when capacity is exhausted without dropping or completing unprocessed messages.
Preserve stable group assignment and FIFO processing.
Register offsets before workers can complete the corresponding work.
items.exampleFix:
for i in range(num_queues):
            work_queue: queue.Queue[WorkItem[T]] = queue.Queue(maxsize=1000)
            self.queues.append(work_queue)

            worker = OrderedQueueWorker[T](
                worker_id=i,
                work_queue=work_queue,
                result_processor=result_processor,
                identifier=identifier,
                offset_tracker=self.offset_tracker,
            )
            worker.start()
            self.workers.append(worker)

    def get_queue_for_group(self, group_key: str) -> int:
        """
        Get queue index for a group using consistent hashing.
        """
        return hash(group_key) % self.num_queues

    def submit(self, group_key: str, work_item: WorkItem[T]) -> None:
        """
        Submit a work item to the appropriate queue.
        """
        queue_index = self.get_queue_for_group(group_key)
        work_queue = self.queues[queue_index]

        self.offset_tracker.add_offset(work_item.partition, work_item.offset)
        work_queue.put(work_item)
items.notes: The capacity is illustrative; other finite positive bounds are valid. Blocking put is explicitly permitted by the finding. Nonblocking rejection needs wider changes because the strategy currently catches submission exceptions and completes their offsets.

items.defectStatement: get_committable_offsets() stops at an integer offset that was never submitted, unnecessarily withholding later completed records across legitimate Kafka gaps. The blockage is not permanent in this implementation: committing and removing the earlier prefix allows a subsequent scan to start beyond the gap.
obligations: Advance across absent offsets when all earlier submitted records have completed.
Stop before any earlier submitted offset that remains outstanding.
Preserve the committed watermark and partition-specific locking.
Return processed offsets using the existing tracker convention, without adding one.
items.notes: Sorting delivered offsets suffices for ordered Kafka partition delivery; a deque is not required. Verified that the original code returns 100, then 103 after mark_committed(100), for completed offsets 100/102/103. Rebalance-state cleanup is a separate issue outside this anchor.

items.defectStatement: OrderedQueueWorker completes each work item's offset in finally even when result_processor raises, including its ShutDown path. Later commits can therefore advance past failed processing and prevent redelivery.
obligations: Complete the offset only when processing succeeds.
Leave failed or interrupted work outstanding so commits cannot advance past it.
Preserve exception logging and the existing ShutDown exit behavior.
Keep queue-depth metrics running on both successful and failed attempts.
items.notes: The trailing finally owns the unchanged metrics.gauge block immediately after the anchor. Moving completion into else avoids needing a success flag outside the replacement range.
